name: Operational / Service Incident
purpose: Replace the legacy WM-ACT-019 physical-emergency boundary with a held operational/service-incident candidate while preserving separate observation, qualification, Problem, Defect, Task and communication masters.

disposition.reason: The retained identifier requires a version above the legacy line and registry-approved migration; this candidate is not publishable.

owns: one incident declaration identity per determined occurrence
severity and revisioned incident impact assertions
containment restoration resolution closure and reopen state/history assertions
delegates: observations and occurrence evidence to WM-MAT-008 and WM-ACT-015
cyber qualification and regulatory clocks to WM-ACT-020
persistent discrepancy problem and root-cause claims to WM-KNW-014
version-pinned product nonconformity to reserved WM-SFT-014
containment restoration and remediation work execution to WM-ACT-006
public or addressed communications to WM-ACT-027
excludes: automatic incident identity from an alert
a second peer incident master for cyber qualification

Incident.rule: One non-withdrawn declaration identity per occurrenceRef; reports remain external until declaration.

ImpactAssessment.rule: Identified revisioned child of exactly one incident; no implicit roll-up to Problem.

IncidentStateTransition.rule: Transitions append; reopening and correction preserve all prior state, impact and review records.

IncidentReview.rule: findings and recommendations may not contain authoritative causal assertions; causal content resolves through typed rootCauseClaimRefs.

IncidentCorrespondence.rule: REFERENCE only; correspondence never proves identity or creates another master.
IncidentCorrespondence.lifecycle: Effective-dated, append-only and correctable; mistaken correspondence closes with validTo and withdrawalReason.

IncidentMerge.rule: Absorbed identity remains addressable through IncidentCorrespondence with role mirror; no history or outbound reference is deleted.

QualificationReference.rule: The peer record cannot hold an independent declaration decision for the same occurrence.

relations.purpose: Resolve occurrence evidence used by declaration.
Resolve cyber qualification under the single-declaration rule.
Resolve persistent problems and their cause claims.
Resolve version-pinned defects; reserved external boundary only.
Resolve containment restoration and remediation tasks.

invariants: INV-001 Observation event alarm or report never becomes an incident without an authorized definition-pinned declaration decision.
INV-002 Among non-withdrawn declarations occurrenceRef is unique; operational cyber and AI qualifications share the governing declarationDecisionId.
INV-003 Cyber-first or operational-first qualification references the governing declarationDecisionId and never creates a peer incident master.
INV-004 If a separate cyber record is retained it requires explicit same-occurrence correspondence with representation role and evidence.
INV-005 Incident Problem Defect Task Communication and observation identities never merge.
INV-006 Severity assessments name their scale and append rather than overwrite.
INV-007 Task priority is independently asserted and is never copied or derived from incident severity.
INV-008 ImpactAssessment is an identified revisioned incident child and distinguishes actual from potential impact.
INV-009 Problem impact is never an implicit roll-up of incident impact.
INV-010 RootCauseClaim is a namespaced Problem child with evidence confidence status and provenance.
INV-011 Supported disputed and other competing cause claims coexist.
INV-012 A cause claim may reference a defect but can never be the defect.
INV-013 WM-SFT-014 defect identity and lifecycle remain external and version pinned.
INV-014 Containment restoration and permanent remediation are separate WM-ACT-006 tasks.
INV-015 Restoration never proves cause elimination or permanent remediation completion.
INV-016 Incident restore resolve close reopen or merge never closes deletes or mutates Problem Defect Task Claim or Communication.
INV-017 Temporary restoration may permit incident closure under incident authority while Problem and permanent remediation remain open.
INV-018 Problem closure requires its own authority and cannot be inferred from incident or task state.
INV-019 Incident state Problem disposition Claim status Defect state and Task state remain independent.
INV-020 Occurrence detection observation declaration restoration ingestion and recording clocks remain distinct.
INV-021 Reopen supersession correction and merge preserve all declaration severity impact resolution review and correspondence history.
INV-022 Correspondence relationship and role assignment do not prove identity execution completion or causation.
INV-023 Unknown missing and stale evidence remain explicit and never mean absence.
INV-024 Personal sensitive and regulated evidence is exposed only through governed projections.
INV-025 No cascade delete crosses aggregate boundaries.
INV-026 Every Reference carries targetModel and targetId; Defect references also carry targetRevision.
INV-027 Incident transitions conform to allowedTransitions; reopen is closed-to-declared.
INV-028 An absorbed incident remains as a mirror correspondence after merge.
INV-029 Authoritative causal assertions never live in free-text IncidentReview findings.
INV-030 A separate qualification record has no independent declaration decision for the same occurrence.
INV-031 Known clocks satisfy occurrence before detection or observation before declaration, and restoration before resolution before closure.
INV-032 Missing source coverage is represented as partial or unknown with a window and staleness state.
INV-033 Incident evidence and affected-subject references carry external classification and disclosure controls before projection.
holds: WM-ACT-019 is a semantic rewrite of a legacy physical-emergency model and requires registry review before publication.
WM-SFT-014 has a reservation but no live complete specification and remains reference-only.
WM-KNW-014 Problem specialization and its incident relations require registry approval.
WM-ACT-034 versus incident-child ImpactAssessment remains an explicit neighbor decision.
Observation-plane identity and the physical/service/cyber/AI incident neighbor set remain unresolved.
Canonical publication runtime search resolve and package verification are pending.
WM-ACT-020 shared-ledger COMPOSE edge conflicts with this REFERENCE boundary and must be corrected before publication.
WM-KNW-014 and WM-SFT-014 share an unpinned parent signal that requires registry adjudication.
WM-ACT-020 remains single-provider or independently waived and is not treated as canonically complete here.
Incident and Problem master-system authorities are not named in the frozen dossier.
A field-level crosswalk for every external reference contract is absent.
WM-AI-010 inbound migration and qualification binding is unresolved.
External registry identifiers for definition/policy catalogue, authority/party, severity scale, unit, residual risk and affected service remain unassigned and no placeholder identifier is minted.
WM-ACT-020 incident-local cause-hypothesis overlap with WM-KNW-014 RootCauseClaim requires registry adjudication.

referenceType.name: Reference

fields.targetModel: required governed model identifier or explicit unassigned registry role
fields.targetRevision: optional except required for Defect references

referenceType.rule: A reference never proves identity, execution, completion or causation.

transitionRules.reopen: Reopen is the closed-to-declared transition with evidence and authority; reopened is not a resting state.
transitionRules.shortcuts: A skipped operational state requires explicit evidence in the transition.
transitionRules.ordering: When known: occurrenceAt <= detectedAt or observedAt <= declaredAt; restoredAt <= resolvedAt <= closedAt. Unknown clocks are explicit and never fabricated.

rootCauseClaim.rule: First-class namespaced child of Problem; competing claims coexist and are never represented by overwriting one root-cause field.

statusHistory.rule: Append-only; supersedesClaimId requires superseded status on the prior claim.

WM-KNW-014.closureRule: Problem closure stays WM-KNW-014-owned and requires its own authority and evidence; this candidate never infers closure.
WM-KNW-014.authority: non-normative neighbor expectation pending WM-KNW-014 registry approval

WM-ACT-020.identityRule: Specializes or qualifies the same incident declaration identity; if an implementation retains a separate record, IncidentCorrespondence is mandatory and the record is not a peer incident master.
WM-ACT-020.authority: non-normative neighbor expectation pending WM-ACT-020 approval
originationRules: Operational-first: WM-ACT-020 qualification references the governing declarationDecisionId and may not create another declaration.
Cyber-first: WM-ACT-020 may originate the sole declaration identity; any later WM-ACT-019 representation is a mirror referencing that declarationDecisionId.
Any retained peer record carries qualificationKind, occurrenceRef and governing declarationDecisionId and has no independent DeclarationDecision.

WM-AI-010.rule: AI incident qualification follows the one-declaration rule; exact binding remains held.

causePromotionRule: Incident-local hypotheses are non-authoritative references only while no Problem exists; once a Problem is opened, claims are mastered as WM-KNW-014 children and the incident retains typed references.
resolutionBinding: Incident status resolved requires an effective ResolutionRecord; closed additionally requires an authorized closed transition.

linkAuthority.incidentProblem: WM-KNW-014 Problem owns association; Incident.problemRefs and ResolutionRecord.problemRefs are projections and must reconcile to it.

reexpressed: emergency state as operational incident transition history
inboundImpacts: WM-AI-010 must follow the one-declaration qualification rule
migration.publicationRule: No migration is canonical until registry review approves the replacement and inbound reference plan.
